prediction_question: Given everything documented about an establishment and its own prior inspections before an inspection begins, which of the 61 violation codes will the inspector record for this visit?
prediction_time: The moment the inspection is opened, before any observation: inspection_date is known when a canvass is scheduled or a complaint triggers a visit, and every intended feature is either a static facility attribute, the inspection's own type, or a field of an earlier inspection of the same licence.
target_definition: The set of violation codes recorded in the row's `violations` blob, parsed into codes 1-70 (multi-label, 61 observed codes; mean 3.08 per inspection). The label source column `violations` is excluded from every shipped file, together with `results` and the per-violation comment text.

split_strategy: Temporal by inspection_date, no random component; three disjoint windows own the train, eval and holdout periods. Measured on the modelling pool (results in Pass/Fail/Pass w/ Conditions AND violations IS NOT NULL): train 2010-01-01..2020-12-31 156,853 rows / 28,930 licences; eval 2021-01-01..2023-12-31 35,360 rows / 12,992 licences; holdout 2024-01-01..2026-09-30 33,920 rows / 12,953 licences. All 37 floor codes (>=1% of a fresh 15,000-row recent scan) are present in every window (probe_splits.py, 2026-09-28). Licence overlap across windows is expected and is the point of the prior-history features; splits are disjoint in time.

novelty_check.theirs: CDPH ships the raw inspections table plus its own deployed BINARY critical-violation forecasting model (Chicago/food-inspections-evaluation, 2015, R) to prioritise canvass scheduling, evaluated in arXiv 1910.04906 (2019). Kaggle and Socrata host mirrors of this same table. No published formulation predicts the set of violation codes.
novelty_check.ours: The multi-label formulation itself: one row per inspection, target = the set of violation codes (61 observed, parsed from the violations blob by code number, never by description string), with an explicit prediction instant at the inspection's opening, a pre-inspection-only feature set (facility attributes, inspection type, calendar position, and the establishment's own prior-inspection history under its license_), and three disjoint temporal windows. No ML-ready package ships this task.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
